name: Sent Queue Fix Plan
description: Fix prompt dispatch accounting so scheduler capacity tracks real active LLM work, the worker uses an Effect-owned dispatch runtime, and the UI clearly separates claimed backlog from live requests.

userStories.title: Introduce claimed and running queue prompt states
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want per-job SQLite queue rows to distinguish claimed prompts from running prompts so local worker backlog no longer masquerades as active LLM work.
acceptanceCriteria: Upgrade the per-job SQLite queue helpers so prompt lifecycle supports `ready -> claimed -> running` instead of overloading `sent` for all non-ready work.
Add explicit helpers for `markPromptAsRunning`, `getClaimedCount`, `getRunningCount`, and `getDispatchCounts` in `src/server/cron/judgmentsJobs/judgmentJobSqliteService.ts`.
Opening an existing job upgrades legacy `sent` rows to `claimed` without losing queue order or existing work.

userStories.title: Recover legacy sent and stale claimed or running prompts safely
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want restart and stale-queue recovery to handle legacy `sent` rows and new `claimed` or `running` rows so worker restarts do not strand work or create duplicate terminal judgments.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend stale queue cleanup and restart recovery so legacy `sent`, new `claimed`, and new `running` rows all requeue idempotently.
Recovery preserves ready-queue ordering and does not duplicate `judged` or `skipped` terminal outcomes after worker restart.
Tests cover stale claim recovery and restart recovery across all three statuses in the SQLite queue helpers.

userStories.title: Build an Effect-owned judgment dispatch runtime
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a scoped Effect dispatcher to own provider queues and worker fibers so prompt dispatch has one clear runtime owner instead of detached cron-launched reducers.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `src/server/cron/judgmentsJobs/judgmentDispatchRuntime.ts` using `Context` or `Layer`, `Effect.gen`, and scoped worker fibers for provider-scoped dispatch.
The dispatcher exposes bounded per-provider queue-capacity and enqueue APIs that the cron can use without spawning detached serial reducers.
Dispatcher shutdown interrupts worker fibers and leaves prompts in a recoverable state during shutdown or writer demotion.
Add `src/server/cron/judgmentsJobs/judgmentDispatchRuntime.test.ts` covering bounded queue behavior, provider-scoped dispatch, and interruption cleanup.

userStories.title: Move prompt lifecycle transitions into Effect acquire or release boundaries
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the dispatcher to own `claimed -> running` and terminal cleanup transitions so success, retry, failure, and interruption all release prompt and request state correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: When a dispatcher worker starts a prompt, it transitions `claimed -> running` inside an `Effect.acquireRelease` boundary.
Success, retry, skip, failure, and interruption release prompt state to `judged`, `ready`, or `skipped` without stranding rows in `running`.
Request runtime accounting still reflects live upstream LLM calls only and continues to compose with provider-scoped request caps.
`src/server/cron/judgmentsJobs/judgmentsRequestRuntime.test.ts` covers release behavior on success, connection failure, and interruption.

userStories.title: Top up scheduler capacity from dispatcher state instead of raw sent rows
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want `judgmentsJobsSendToLLM.ts` to compute deficits from real request activity and bounded dispatcher capacity so Forska claims only the work it can actively drain.
acceptanceCriteria: Update `src/server/cron/judgmentsJobs/judgmentsJobsSendToLLM.ts` so per-provider deficits are computed from actual request runtime activity plus available dispatcher queue capacity.
The cron claims only enough prompts to fill the bounded local dispatcher buffer instead of filling an entire provider-cap worth of local backlog.
Jobs sharing one provider connection still make fair progress, and different provider connections can still advance independently under shared caps.
`src/server/cron/judgmentsJobs/judgmentsJobsSendToLLM.test.ts` verifies scheduler top-up uses dispatcher capacity rather than counting every claimed prompt as running.

userStories.title: Expose claimed and running prompt stats in job APIs
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the job detail API and client defaults to expose prompt backlog and request activity separately so server and client code stop treating claimed prompts as active LLM calls.
acceptanceCriteria: Update `src/server/routes/JudgmentsJobsRoutes.ts` to return prompt-level counts using `claimed` and `running` names while keeping `requestStats.inFlight` for actual live LLM calls.
Update `src/services/judgmentsJobsService.ts` defaults and related client types to match the renamed prompt stats payload.
`src/server/routes/JudgmentsJobsRoutes.test.ts` covers the renamed prompt stats and keeps `requestStats.inFlight` semantics unchanged.

userStories.title: Clarify queue backlog versus request activity in the admin UI
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the admin job UI to distinguish claimed backlog, running prompts, and active LLM calls so I can understand whether Forska or the runtime is the bottleneck.
acceptanceCriteria: Update `/admin/jobs/:id` so the queue card shows `Ready`, `Claimed`, `Running Prompts`, `Judged`, and `Skipped` instead of the old `Prompts in Progress` wording.
Update the request activity card to show `Active LLM Calls` and `Attempts`, with copy that makes clear those numbers are request-level rather than prompt-level.
Rename or tooltip the nav waiting or running indicator so it is clearly described as runtime-only LLM waiting and running data.

Browser verify `/admin/jobs/:id`: local queue card shows `Ready`, `Claimed`, `Running Prompts`, `Judged`, and `Skipped`; request activity shows `Active LLM Calls` and `Attempts`; nav indicator still reflects runtime-only waiting or running
